headline: Bitcoin mining data center condemned after leaking 3M gallons of water, operating illegally
summary: A Bitcoin mining data center in El Reno, Oklahoma, was condemned after leaking 3 million gallons of water, forcing school and business closures. It had been operating under a city stop-work order since 2023 due to safety code violations.
details: A Bitcoin mining data center in El Reno, Oklahoma, has been condemned after leaking 3 million gallons of water. This massive leak forced the closure of schools, businesses, and city offices last week in the area.

The facility, owned by Athlon Blockchain LLC, was reportedly operating illegally. The city had issued a Stop Work Order in 2023 due to multiple fire and life safety code violations and expired permits.

Despite the order, the firm is believed to have set up the data center and commenced operations without city consultation, possibly housing it in shipping containers to sidestep regulations. The city asserts that no costs related to the leak will be passed on to citizens and is preparing legal action to recoup expenses from the property owner.

This incident highlights growing concerns over data center water usage, especially amid widespread drought conditions. Regulators are now committed to routinely reviewing compliance to prevent similar environmental and public safety repercussions.
